record.original_question: For the unrestricted partition generating function product over m >= 1 of (1 + x^m + x^(2m) + ...), can one choose signs in some of the factors so that, after expansion, every coefficient belongs to {0, -1, 1}?

evidence.quote: Question: can we change some of the signs above into minus signs so that the bn’s are also in {0, ±1}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the formal power series identity
$$\prod_{m\ge 1}\bigl(1+x^m+x^{2m}+x^{3m}+\cdots\bigr)=\sum_{n\ge 0}p(n)\,x^n,$$
where $p(n)$ is the number of unrestricted integer partitions of $n$. For each $m\ge 1$ and each $k\ge 1$, let $\varepsilon_{m,k}\in\{+1,-1\}$, and consider the "signed" infinite product
$$F(x)=\prod_{m\ge 1}\Bigl(1+\sum_{k\ge 1}\varepsilon_{m,k}\,x^{km}\Bigr)=\sum_{n\ge 0}b_n\,x^n\in\mathbb{Z}[[x]].$$
(Each coefficient $b_n$ is a finite sum since only finitely many factors contribute to the coefficient of $x^n$.)

Question: Does there exist a choice of signs $\{\varepsilon_{m,k}\}_{m\ge 1,\,k\ge 1}$, with $\varepsilon_{m,k}\in\{+1,-1\}$, such that $b_n\in\{-1,0,+1\}$ for every $n\ge 0$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of this sign-choice problem for the partition generating function. Related work on sign patterns in infinite products (e.g., the Borwein-type products) addresses different questions, and no source confirming a solution—positive or negative—was located.

status_evidence.title: Some conjectures of Schlosser and Zhou on sign patterns of the coefficients of infinite products
status_evidence.snippet: Studies sign patterns of coefficients in q-series expansions of infinite products such as (q;q)_infty/(q^p;q^p)_infty, but does not address choosing signs to force coefficients into {0,±1} for the unrestricted partition product.
status_evidence.claim: Related sign-pattern literature does not resolve the stated sign-choice problem.
